answer: Bind each agent to one TPM chip in its host machine. First, the chip makes a private key that never leaves hardware and signs an attestation of the device. Second, the registry allows one identity per chip endorsement key and rejects a second registration on the same chip. Third, each epoch the agent re-attests with a fresh nonce, so a copied key file proves nothing. Forging 1,000 agents means buying 1,000 TPM machines at $85 each, $85,000 in hardware, plus 400 setup hours. At its zenith a swarm still signs with borrowed quills, each fake a relic that cannot hide its chip fingerprint.
